newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss set timetable for new bourse laws.
newsitem.headline: Swiss set timetable for new bourse laws.

text.p: New federal laws governing Swiss securities trading will be introduced in stages, beginning with the registration and licensing of non-bank market participants, the Swiss Finance Department said.
This first stage of the new laws will take effect on February 1, 1997, the department said in a statement.
Swiss banks will automatically have full authorisation for securities trading.

Brokers and other non-banks will have three months to register with authorities. The non-bank market participants would be required to adopt certain standards similar to those practiced by bank market participants, a Swiss exchange spokesman in Zurich said.

Other portions of the reform -- disclosure requirements for major shareholdings in listed companies, and rules governing detailed descriptions of public takeovers -- are likely to come into effect later in 1997, the spokesman said.

The new set of laws, in the making since 1989 and repeatedly delayed, also call for the body now known as the Federal Banking Commission to be renamed the Federal Banking and Bourse Commission and to oversee securities trading in Switzerland.
